rawFindings.title: Possible crash when slug is a number without toString()
rawFindings.explanation: In the original code, slugize is called with (data.slug || data.title).toString() to ensure the input is a string. The patched line removes toString(), which can cause a crash if data.slug or data.title is a number or other non-string object without a suitable toString method.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore .toString() to ensure the input to slugize is always a string: data.slug = slugize((data.slug || data.title).toString(), {transform: config.filename_case});

rawFindings.title: Potential crash when data.slug is a number without toString() in publish()
rawFindings.explanation: The patch changes slugize(data.slug.toString(), {...}) to slugize(data.slug, {...}). If data.slug is a number, this will cause slugize to throw, because it expects a string. The original code safely converts it to string before slugizing.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore .toString() call when slugizing data.slug in publish(): var slug = data.slug = slugize(data.slug.toString(), {transform: config.filename_case});
